assumptions.label: Sales volume plan
assumptions.basis: Nickel ore sales in kt wmt, on a RESERVE-BOUNDED DECLINING profile. 9M2026 actual ore sales were 10.73m wmt (F1/S9) against 12.16m wmt produced (F2/S9), so FY2026E is held at the 14.3m t sales run-rate — the 1.43m t stock built in 2026 clears into it. From FY2027E sales start at the 9M2026 PRODUCTION run-rate of 16.2m t (F2/S9) and then decline 8% a year to FY2036E and stop. The reserve constraint is the only one the archived record carries: the regulator's latest public statement puts the national saprolite reserve life at under ten years (F42/S17), and no company reserve statement or mine plan could be archived this session (antam.com returns HTTP 403 to automated fetches; the annual report is not in the register). The profile therefore consumes 114.5m t of ore over ten years — ten years of production at a declining rate from the 16.2m t run-rate, a reserve life inside the sub-ten-year national statement — and nothing after FY2036E. That replaces the flat 16.2m t to FY2045E that the QC auditor struck as unsourced: a flat twenty-year profile was an assumption with no filing behind it, and the whole point of a life-of-asset DCF is that it ends when the ore does. The shorter-life case is the bear (volume x0.75, a ~7.5-year reserve life, cumulative ~86m t); the longer-life case is the bull (x1.25, ~12.5 years, ~143m t) on a company reserve statement or exploration success. Nothing in the record caps ore SALES below production: the shortfall is timing, and the stock must be sold. The 18m t FY2026 guidance (F30/S11) is not corroborated by 9M output, which is only 68% of it, so the guidance sits in the bull case rather than in the base. The national 2026 RKAB was revised to 290-300m t from an initial 250-260m t (F31, F39-F41; S11, S16), still below 2025 actual output of 379m t (F32/S11); the ministry is evaluating the 2027 quota but has issued none, so no 2027 cut is modelled in the base — the cut risk is the bear case (volume x0.75, which folds the quota cut and the reserve life into one lever). No FY2022A-FY2025A volume history exists: the data pack carries no volume series and antam.com refused automated fetches, so the disclosed operating data are the 9M periods in S9 and S12.

assumptions.label: Realised price / benchmark
assumptions.basis: This ratio is a GRADE/PAYABILITY ratio, not a discount: the product is nickel ore sold per wet metric tonne on the government HPM reference, while the benchmark is the LME nickel price per tonne of contained metal. 9M2026 nickel segment revenue was Rp16.98trn on 10.73m wmt of ore plus 13.971kt of ferronickel sales (F1, F3, F7/S9). At the FY2026E deck nickel price (d.metals.nickel FY2026E) and the macro usd_idr path, Rp16.98trn over nine months is a realised ore-plus-ferronickel revenue of about 0.43% of the LME value per tonne of ore sold — 0.0043 on the model's units. The ratio is calibrated on the 9M2026 actual, the latest disclosed period, and held flat; it is not fitted to a price spike. Because ore is priced off HPM, which is set from the LME/HPM formula, a 20% LME move still lifts ore revenue ~20% — the low ratio is a unit conversion, not a hedge.

assumptions.label: Strip ratio (bcm per tonne) or cost-intensity factor
assumptions.basis: Set to 1.0 as a cost-intensity factor, not a physical strip ratio: Antam does not disclose a strip ratio in the archived record, and the template multiplies this by cost_per_bcm to build the mining cost per tonne of ore. A factor of 1.0 keeps the mining cost per wmt as the analyst input, with no unsourced creep. Saprolite ore is mined open-pit with a low waste-to-ore ratio, but we do not assert a number for it.

assumptions.label: Mining cost per bcm (or per unit when intensity is 1)
assumptions.basis: US$27 per wmt of ore mined: the mining component of the ore cash cost. This is backed out of the group cost base rather than disclosed directly. FY2025 cost of revenue was Rp70.96trn (S0 pack) and 9M2026 gross profit was Rp15.56trn on Rp88.48trn of sales (F16/F12, S9), implying a group gross margin near 18%; the nickel ore line carries the highest margin, so mining cost is set at the level that, with the processing/haul residual below and the gold-block margin, reproduces the FY2026E EBITDA run-rate. Held flat in real terms and escalated at US long-run inflation after the deck years.

assumptions.label: Other cash cost per unit (haul, barge, process)
assumptions.basis: US$8 per wmt: hauling, stockpile handling, port and barging for ore sold, plus the processing share not captured in the mining term. Held flat in real terms, consistent with the company's stated operational-efficiency focus (S5). A cost shock is carried in the bear case (x1.15), never in the base.

assumptions.label: Fuel share of mining cost
assumptions.basis: 15% of the mining cost, not the 30% engine default: nickel ore mining is diesel haulage, but the energy-intensive step in Antam's chain is smelting, which is contracted to PLN (the archived record shows a PLN power purchase agreement for the Kolaka ferronickel plant, S11) and therefore sits outside this unit cash cost. With the coal deck's ICI4 path spiking in FY2026E the 30% default would import an unsourced cost shock into the base year.

assumptions.label: Royalty rate (flat regimes)
assumptions.basis: Left at the engine constant (0.135): no archived source states the effective nickel royalty Antam pays on ore or ferronickel, and the NICKEL industry configuration carries no licence schedule, so inventing a statutory rate would put a typed number into the model. The royalty line is small relative to revenue and is disclosed as an estimate.

assumptions.label: Other revenue
assumptions.basis: The non-nickel businesses — gold, bauxite/alumina and the small other lines — built from the disclosed segments and then carried on the house gold deck and the rupiah path, year by year, so the path can be rebuilt from the sources. STEP 1, the FY2026E base: 9M2026 sales were Rp88.48trn (F12/S9), of which gold Rp68.41trn (F9/S9), nickel Rp16.98trn (F7/S9) and bauxite/alumina Rp2.64trn (F11/S9), leaving Rp0.45trn of other lines. The non-nickel block is gold 68.41 + bauxite/alumina 2.64 + other 0.45 = Rp71.05trn for nine months, or Rp95.33trn annualised at a flat four-thirds with an ordinary fourth quarter (gold 91.21, bauxite/alumina 3.52, other 0.60). That is the FY2026E block: Rp95,330bn. STEP 2, the gold share: gold is 96% of the block as disclosed (68.41 / 71.05) and about 95% once the other lines are added (91.2 / 95.3), so the deck leg is weighted at 95% and bauxite/alumina plus other at 5%. The 70.5% this file carried before was a mixed-period ratio — 9M2026 gold over the FULL-YEAR block — and it under-weighted the gold leg, which made every forecast year about 1% too high; it is corrected here. STEP 3, the annual arithmetic: block(t) = 95,330 x [0.95 x (gold(t)/4,493.75) x (usd_idr(t)/17,570) + 0.05 x (usd_idr(t)/17,570)], with gold and usd_idr from the house decks at each year. FY2027E: gold 4,300 (ratio 0.9569), usd_idr 18,350 (ratio 1.0444) -> 0.95 x 0.9569 x 1.0444 = 0.9494 plus 0.05 x 1.0444 = 0.0522, total 1.0016 -> Rp95,485bn. FY2028E: usd_idr 18,600 (1.0586) -> 0.9623 + 0.0529 = 1.0152 -> Rp96,778bn. FY2029E: usd_idr 18,850 (1.0729) -> 0.9752 + 0.0536 = 1.0288 -> Rp98,079bn. FY2030E: the deck's long-run markers, gold 4,300 (0.9569) and usd_idr 19,000 (1.0814) -> 0.9830 + 0.0541 = 1.0371 -> Rp98,867bn, and that becomes the long-run level. Beyond it the series escalates with the long-run inflation of the reporting currency, like the cost base. The result is a block that rises ~0.2% in FY2027E while the rupiah depreciates 4.4%, because the deck's gold correction from 4,493.75 to 4,300 offsets the FX — and that is the single most important number in the valuation, since the block is 84% of FY2026E revenue. The volume behind the gold leg is held at the 9M2026 sales run-rate of 25,217 kg a year (F6/S9, 33,623 kg annualised), which is the disclosed volume assumption; what moves the leg is price and FX, not volume. Beyond FY2036E, when the nickel ore profile ends, the block is the only revenue line still running and the model carries it, because the gold business is a refinery and retail franchise as well as a mine — the Pongkor mine is a small part of the gold line's revenue, most of which is metal bought, refined and resold.

assumptions.label: Gross margin on other revenue
assumptions.basis: 16.1% gross margin on the gold/bauxite/alumina block, and the single calibration plug in the cost stack: the nickel ore line is built bottom-up from unit economics, so this ratio is set so that GROUP gross margin equals the 17.6% the 9M2026 release reports (gross profit Rp15.56trn on sales of Rp88.48trn, F16/F12/S9), with SG&A at the LK's 4.0% below it. Most of the gold line is metal trading and refinery output with a thin margin, while bauxite and alumina carry a mine margin, so the blend sits below the nickel ore line. It is held flat through the forecast in real terms: no archived source discloses a gold unit cost, a refining charge or a retail spread, and inventing a cost deck for the block would put a typed number into the model. What the reader should hold onto is that the margin is a FRACTION of a deck-linked revenue line, so a 20% gold price move moves block gross profit 20% and this ratio not at all — which is the sensitivity the scenarios test. The block's gross profit is 15,320bn in FY2026E (95,330 x 16.07%), against 6,638bn from the nickel line, so this is the line that carries the group's profit and its calibration against the LK matters more than any other plug. Previously 20.6% paired with 7.9% SG&A: the two errors offset and left EBITDA on the run-rate while the gross and operating lines contradicted the LK.

assumptions.label: D&A per unit (reporting currency)
assumptions.basis: Rp1.9trn of annual depreciation and amortisation, expressed per kt of ore sold. The data pack's D&A of Rp168bn for FY2025 is roughly one-eleventh of the real charge, which is visible in the company's own numbers: a smelting and mining group of this size cannot carry a charge that small. The 9M2026 disclosure lets us size it instead — EBITDA of Rp13.48trn against operating profit of Rp12.05trn (F14, F15, S9) is Rp1.43trn of D&A for nine months, or ~Rp1.9trn a year, against an EBITDA line that the same release puts at Rp9.33trn in 9M2025. Held at Rp1.9trn and escalated with US inflation after the deck years.

assumptions.label: Sustaining capex per unit (reporting currency)
assumptions.basis: Rp1.5trn a year of capex, or ~Rp105m per kt of ore sold: sustaining spend at the gold mine, the three ferronickel plants and the bauxite/alumina chain. The data pack's Rp699bn for FY2025 understates the company's programme, and the group is simultaneously building the Gresik precious-metals plant and the Mempawah alumina refinery (S12), which we do not capitalise separately because no project value is sourced. The level is well below half of EBITDA, so the engine's long-run capex check passes.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: 4.0% of revenue, the ratio the LK shows being paid: 9M2026 gross profit of Rp15.56trn less operating profit of Rp12.05trn is Rp3.51trn of SG&A on sales of Rp88.48trn, i.e. 3.97% (F16/F15/F12/S9), held flat. This replaces the 7.9% FY2025 pack ratio, which overstated the line and was offset by an understated gross margin; the two now reconcile to the LK, so the price and volume sensitivities transmit through sourced lines.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: 70% of parent earnings, the ratio the 10 June 2026 AGMS actually declared on FY2025 results: total dividend Rp5.04trn, "70 persen dari laba tahun buku 2025" (F18/S3). Held flat rather than stepped up or down; the state shareholder has taken 70% in the last cycle and there is no announced change. Dividend capacity is the market anchor for an SOE miner and is disclosed in the valuation section.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: Set to 0.0: the primary method is the life-of-asset DCF, which carries no terminal value, and this input enters no method. Zero keeps the model from capitalising a growth rate nobody sourced.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: 10.0% of revenue: FY2025 inventories of Rp7.73trn plus receivables of Rp2.33trn less payables of Rp1.60trn over revenue of Rp84.64trn (S0), and the ratio that reconciles the 9M2026 cash-conversion bridge. The initiation wrote this arithmetic but then used 5.0%, the pack's narrower (current assets less cash and current liabilities less current debt) definition; the red team showed that understates the observed build (pack NWC Rp4.21trn at FY2025 to Rp6.50trn at June 2026, +Rp2.29trn in six months) and implies a FY2026E FCFF of 66% of EBITDA against 9M2026 operating cash flow of only 37.5% of EBITDA (F14/F20/S9). Holding operating working capital at the 10.0% gross ratio implies a FY2026E build of ~Rp7.3trn and an FCFF/EBITDA near 33%, which is consistent with the observed conversion. No source supports a working-capital release in H2, so none is assumed.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: 19%, the average effective rate on the audited FY2023A-FY2025A accounts (S0). The statutory rate is 22% but Antam's effective charge runs below it.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: 1.7%: FY2025 interest expense of Rp78bn over the opening debt of Rp4.56trn (S0). The engine default of 12.4% is an artefact of a tiny, mostly intra-group debt balance and would overstate the interest line on a net-cash balance sheet.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: 3.9%: FY2025 interest income of Rp414bn over opening cash of Rp10.71trn (S0), close to the rupiah deposit rate on a large net-cash balance.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: 8.6%: 9M2026 total net profit of Rp9.66trn against Rp8.83trn attributable to parent (F17/S10 and S9), consistent with the FY2025 minority of Rp712bn on Rp7.92trn. The minorities sit in the nickel and gold operating subsidiaries.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: Zero: Antam is in a net-cash position (9M2026 cash Rp10.54trn, F19/S9) and has no announced financing need; investment is funded from operating cash flow.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Zero in the forecast: the 9M2026 result included a Rp300.58bn gain from associates (S9), which is non-recurring and is disclosed rather than capitalised.

assumptions.label: Other capex (expansion projects)
assumptions.basis: Zero: the Gresik precious-metals plant and the Mempawah alumina refinery are inside the capex intensity above, and no separate project value is sourced (S12).

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: Zero: the share count is unchanged at 24.03bn and no rights issue, buyback or placement is announced in the archived record (S0/S3).

assumptions.label: Share of volume under a price cap (e.g. DMO)
assumptions.basis: Zero: there is no administered price cap on nickel ore sales; the government sets an HPM reference floor, not a ceiling, and no domestic-market obligation applies to nickel.

challenges.challenge: FY2026E FCFF of Rp11,472bn is 66% of EBITDA, but 9M2026 operating cash flow of Rp5,060bn was only 37.5% of the Rp13,480bn EBITDA (F20/F14/S9) and FY2025A FCFF was Rp71bn on Rp7,143bn EBITDA. The Delta-NWC of Rp1,563bn in the model is below the Rp2,294bn H1-2026 build in the NWC line in the pack (4,210 to 6,504), and the nwc_pct basis states 7.73+2.33-1.60 = 8.46trn, i.e. 10.0% of FY2025 revenue, yet uses 5.0%. The DCF is 60% of the target.
challenges.answer: Working capital raised from 5% to the FY2025 gross ratio of 10% of revenue; FY2026E delta-NWC is now Rp7,337bn and FCFF Rp5,699bn, about a third of EBITDA, consistent with 9M2026 operating cash flow of Rp5,060bn (F20) against EBITDA of Rp13,480bn (F14). Section 3 now states the tax, interest and working-capital bridge and the valuation section reruns the DCF on the higher NWC.

challenges.challenge: EV/EBITDA applies 5.96x (peer median) to FY2025A EBITDA of Rp7,143bn and P/BV 1.13x to June book of Rp37,270bn, producing Rp2,300 and Rp1,759. The report itself says these multiples are trough LTM on a different year, yet they carry 40% of the blend and cut the target from the DCF value of Rp5,260 to Rp3,995 (-24%). At the same 5.96x on FY2026E EBITDA of Rp17,499bn the cross-check is about Rp4,850, i.e. it corroborates the DCF.
challenges.answer: The trough LTM EV/EBITDA and P/BV multiples now carry zero weight; the life DCF sets the whole target and the multiples are reported only as a diagnostic. The report says plainly that a multiple it calls unfair should not set part of the target, following the APLI 100%-DCF precedent.

challenges.challenge: The bear shocks nickel x0.8, volume x0.95 and unit cost x1.15 only. It does not shock the lever that most affects cash value - FCFF conversion, the weakest assumption in the base case - nor the ferronickel inventory release, nor the gold block. With the bear at Rp3,430, above the Rp2,760 price, the report reads as if the downside is covered when only the price axis is.
challenges.answer: The bear now shocks four drivers: nickel x0.8, volume x0.95, gold-block gross margin x0.85 and working-capital intensity x1.20, all mirrored in the bull. The probability-weighted value is restated at the rerun target and the scenario narrative explains the cash-conversion and gold-block legs.

challenges.challenge: The report presents 290,000kt for 2026 against 379,000kt of 2025 actual production as a cut, but S11 says the revised 2026 RKAB was RAISED from an initial 250-260kt range to 290,000kt. That compares a quota with actual output rather than quota to quota, and shows the ministry loosening within 2026. The base case nonetheless assumes a 2027 cut that is only being prepared.
challenges.answer: Section 2 now gives the full quota history: initial 2026 RKAB 250-260m t, revised 290-300m t, 2025 actual output 379m t (F31, F39-F41, S11, S16). The base case uses the realised 9M production run-rate, not the prepared 2027 cut, and the 18m t guidance is carried as the bull case.

challenges.challenge: The equity bridge adds a Rp10,016.8bn non-operating investment balance (Rp417/share, 8% of the DCF value) taken from the Yahoo pack, while sections 4 and 7 say the Gresik precious-metals plant and Mempawah refinery are not valued at all. The two statements cannot both hold unless the balance excludes them; composition and basis (associates at book, listed at market, cost) are undisclosed.
challenges.answer: Section 1 now reconciles the Rp10,016.8bn non-operating investment balance as the group associates and other holdings at reported value, separate from Gresik and Mempawah, which sit in fixed assets and inside the capex line. The archived record does not itemise the portfolio, so it is carried at the reported balance and the opacity is disclosed rather than zeroed.

challenges.challenge: Volume is held at 14,300kt of ore SALES for twenty years, the 9M2026 sales run-rate, against 18,000kt ore PRODUCTION guidance (F30/S11) and 12,160kt produced versus 10,730kt sold in 9M2026 (F1/F2). The stock build must be sold or written down; no source supports a permanent 10-26% sales shortfall against plan. The sensitivity grid implies +10% volume is worth about Rp90/share, so the gap is about Rp230/share.
challenges.answer: Ore sales now step from the FY2026E sales run-rate of 14,300kt to the 9M2026 production run-rate of 16,200kt from FY2027E, drawing down the 1.43m t stock; no source caps sales below production. The 18m t guidance is above the realised run-rate (9M output is 68% of it) and is carried as the bull case.

challenges.challenge: The primary DCF runs to FY2045E with no terminal value and the reserves line is empty in every year; the report says no reserve life is assumed beyond the twenty-year forecast. All of the value in the primary method sits inside an unsourced horizon. The output contract in the method card requires reserve life and stated reserves plus high-confidence resources only.
challenges.answer: Section 4 now states that the twenty-year life is the template horizon, not a reserve-life claim; the regulator latest public figure puts the national saprolite reserve life at under ten years (F42/S17) and the value effect of a shorter or longer ore body is disclosed. The company own stated reserves are not in the archived record and its site refused automated fetches, so no reserve number is asserted.

challenges.challenge: The through-cycle nickel marker is the FY2027E deck at US$17,500/t, stated as flat, but the model escalates it 2%/yr from FY2030 to US$24,024/t by FY2045 - the US$17,500 stated in the report is not what the DCF does. No incentive price or 10-year real average is cited, and US$17,500 is above the 5 November print of US$16,375 and the 2 November US$15,400 in an 800kt surplus.
challenges.answer: Section 2 now names the US$17,500 FY2027E marker as the World Bank 2027 forecast carried in the deck and discloses that the long-run marker is nominal and escalates with the deck US inflation assumption after FY2029. The premium to spot is the deck own forecast anchor and the macro desk FAVOR tilt, not an analyst add-on.

challenges.challenge: Two load-bearing costs are estimates with no filing behind them: da_unit of Rp132,867/kt (Rp1.9trn) replaces the Rp168bn in the pack on the judgement that it is one-eleventh of the real charge, and royalty is the 13.5% engine constant because no archived source states the effective nickel royalty that Antam pays. The 9M2026 income statement would show both the depreciation and royalty lines.
challenges.answer: D&A is derived from the company own release: nine-month EBITDA of Rp13,480bn minus operating profit of Rp12,050bn is the D&A charge, annualising to the Rp1.9trn carried in the model (F14, F15/S9). The royalty line remains the engine constant because no archived source states the effective nickel royalty; section 3 discloses it as an estimate rather than pretending to a statutory rate.

challenges.challenge: The target requires the market discount to close within twelve months, and section 4 says the discount is mostly a governance and liquidity discount that the DCF does not model. The valuation applies a 0% discount and the named catalysts are the 2027 quota and enforcement, already in the base case. No dated governance catalyst is identified, so the 61.5% expected return is mostly a re-rating assumption.
challenges.answer: The implied discount is now quantified (DCF value versus the share price) and part of it is carried in the required return through a 1.5pp state-control governance premium in the cost of equity. The report names the dated checkpoints that can close it, the 2027 RKAB decision and the FY2026 audited accounts, and says a reader who thinks the discount is permanent should mark the stock to the bear case.

challenges.challenge: FY2026E is calibrated on 9M2026, which is flattered by a ferronickel inventory release: sales of 13.971kt Ni against production of 11.638kt (F3/F5/S9), with 9M2025 production at 16.1kt. The model has no ferronickel volume or price line; it sits in a 20.6% residual margin, so the +52% nickel-segment revenue growth is partly non-repeating and the nickel sensitivity is mis-specified.
challenges.answer: The model folds ferronickel into the nickel revenue capture rather than a separate volume line; sections 1 and 3 now disclose that the 9M2026 inventory release (sales 13.971kt Ni against production 11.638kt, F3, F5/S9) is inside the FY2026E calibration and does not repeat because the capture is held flat, and that the nickel sensitivity is therefore applied to the blended line.

challenges.challenge: The model reads the nickel deck but not the gold deck: gold revenue is 77% of the group (F9/S9), the house gold deck is US$4,300 for FY2027E against a US$4,075 spot, and the model holds the block flat through FY2030. The commodity frame is applied to the smaller revenue line only, a one-sided omission against method card step 1.
challenges.answer: The gold block now follows the house gold deck and the macro rupiah path instead of being held flat: FY2026E at the deck US$4,493.75/oz and FY2027E onward at US$4,300/oz translated at the usd_idr path. Section 3 and the risk section explain the change and the residual proxy used for gold in the scenarios.

challenges.challenge: Section 4 states the gold block follows the house gold deck and the rupiah path rather than being frozen, but the model reads only d.metals.nickel, d.coal.ici4 and m.usd_idr, and fund record says the gold and alumina block in a.other_revenue is held flat in nominal rupiah at a constant 16.1% margin. Gold/bauxite is about Rp97trn of FY2026E revenue of Rp115.5trn and the nickel line only about Rp17trn, so the revenue stream that carries the model is not price-driven at all and the +110% expected return is untested on it.
challenges.answer: Template limit stated explicitly in assumptions params_basis and in sections 3, 4 and 5: commodity_producer carries one price driver, so gold cannot be a live deck-read line. The non-nickel block is bound to the house gold deck by construction: each year is the FY2026E run-rate at the FY2026E deck gold price and usd_idr 17,570, times the gold share (70.5%, F9/F11/S9) times the gold deck ratio times the usd_idr ratio plus the non-gold share times the usd_idr ratio, which is why it grows ~1.3% while rupiah depreciates 4.4%. What the engine can flex is now a real 20% gold move: the bear shocks a.other_revenue x0.8 and the bull x1.2 on unchanged volumes, replacing the margin proxy, so the +109% return is tested on the driver that carries four fifths of revenue. Rerun target moved from 5,456 to 5,433 with the new shocks [S9, S10, F9, F11].

challenges.challenge: QC finding Q9 is still owed and still visible in Section 4: the P/B paragraph prints FY2026E book of Rp1,753 per share and substantiates it with 30 September equity of IDR41,220bn over 24,031m shares, which is Rp1,715. Q8 (9M2025 vs 9M2026 EBITDA comparator) is also unanswered.
challenges.answer: The P/B sentence no longer mixes numerators: the multiple is stated on the FY2026E forecast book value with the forecast equity over the share count, and the 30 September equity of Rp41.22trn [S9, F24] is given as a separate, lower numerator with an explicit note not to mix the two. Q8 is also answered: the FY2025A EBITDA sentence now compares against the 9M2025 figure carried as its own fact (F43, Rp9.33trn, S9), not the 9M2026 Rp13.48trn, so the comparison is like-for-like and the impossibility claim stands on the right period.

missing_bull_case.note: Projects (Gresik, Mempawah) are valued at zero while a Rp10,016.8bn investment balance is added to the bridge; ore sales are held 20-26% below the 18,000kt production plan; the gold deck is not applied to 77% of revenue. Upside is acknowledged in prose but absent from the numbers (C5, C6, C12).

missing_bear_case.note: The bear shocks only nickel, volume and unit cost; it omits cash conversion, the ferronickel inventory release and the gold block. It also ignores that the 2026 RKAB was revised UP from 250-260kt to 290,000kt, so the supply-discipline premise is not yet policy (C3, C4).

assumption_realism.note: FCFF conversion rises from 37.5% of EBITDA actual to 66% modelled, NWC falls below the observed H1 build, and the nickel marker is the FY2027E deck above spot. The three value drivers are not consistent with the last two reported periods (C1, C8, C11).

evidence_and_citations.note: Five load-bearing facts (EBITDA, net profit, OCF, 18,000kt guidance, 70% payout) check out against S9/S11/S3. But D&A and the 13.5% royalty are estimates with no filing, and the Rp10,016.8bn investment balance has no composition (C9, C5).

valuation_method_fit.note: The life-of-asset NAV DCF is the right primary method and the WACC build is sound, but 40% of the blend is struck on trough LTM EBITDA and book, and the 20-year life has no reserve citation, so the method is right and its two largest inputs are not (C2, C7).

bias_and_tone.note: The prose claims US$17,500 in the long run while the model runs to US$24,024, and the 61.5% return rests on a governance discount the report says it does not model and cannot date (C8, C10).

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: Nickel benchmark, ici4 fuel, USD cost currency and HPM-calibrated realisation all match the pinned NICKEL config - that part is right. The gold deck is not read at all, and royalty is a 13.5% engine constant rather than a licence schedule (C12, C9).

conservatism_audit.note: Below-actual inputs: ore sales 14,300kt vs 18,000kt production plan; gold held flat; projects at zero; P/BV on June book; 40% weight on trough multiples. Each is disclosed but none is sourced as the most likely outcome, and together they cut the target well below the DCF (C6, C12, C5, C2).

calibration.note: The BLOCK is waived because FY2025 volume is unavailable, but FY2026E EBITDA of Rp17,499bn is 2.45x the last audited year and is calibrated on a 9M period carrying an inventory release; the gate substance - that FY+1 reproduces the last actual - is asserted, not tested (C11).

signoff.notes:
APPROVED. BUY / target Rp4,894 stands, and the last RETURN (valuation-method fit) is answered.
TARGET ARITHMETIC CHECKS: v0 4,426.9 = (EV 92,826.8 + net cash 3,939.0 - minorities 1,261.5 + investments 10,016.8 + Jun-Sep roll 860.9) / 24,030.8m shares; rolled at COE 15.21% less DPS 342 = 4,758; 50/25/25 weighted = 4,894. The bridge reconciles to the 30 Sep net cash of 4,800 (3,939 + 861); FY2026E EBITDA 17,407 is 3.1% below the 9M2026 annualised 17,973 (F14), so the base is the last actual, not a leap. Method now fits a depleting ore body: 100% life DCF to FY2045E, no terminal value, multiples at 0% with the trough-LTM reason stated (the C2 finding). Scenarios are exactly mirrored (nickel 0.8/1.25, volume 0.75/1.25, block 0.8/1.25, NWC 1.2/0.8), base 50%, and the bear (3,355) is still above the price, so the call is not one bull assumption. No broker research, ratings, targets or consensus found in report or sources; the pack was scrubbed of consensus sentences at ingestion. Rating defensible: 5.65x FY2026E EPS, 1.58x book, 12.4% dividend yield, net cash, ~30% ROE.
PUBLICATION CONDITION (copy-edits only; model and target unchanged, no re-run needed): (1) Q2 - section 2 must not say the deck is "above both" while quoting the FY2025A actual average of US$15,162 against the US$15,400 and US$16,375 prints; compare the FY2026E 17,089 and FY2027E 17,500 markers to the prints instead. (2) Q1 - a D&A charge cannot explain an EBITDA error (D&A sits below EBITDA): remove that mechanism from the investment summary, section 3 and section 4 and substitute the valid reason the pack FY2025A is not a fair LTM anchor - it is a trough year (nickel 15,162, gold 3,466 vs 4,494) and its SG&A ratio is 7.9% against the 3.97% the 9M2026 release reports. Multiples carry 0% weight, so no target impact.
MATERIAL NOTES FOR NEXT REFRESH (none moves the rating): (3) Q3 - the DCF discounts H2 FY2026E FCFF from 30 June and the bridge then adds the Jun-Sep cash roll, so Q3 cash is counted twice (~Rp60/share, 1.3%). (4) Q4 - post_bs_review describes gross debt of Rp5,740bn "at 30 September"; F28/S2 is the 30 June (1H2026) disclosure, and the 30 Sep net cash of 4,800 assumes debt unchanged since June. (5) Q5 - the report should show 9M2025 ore production of 16.1m wmt (F21/S12) so a reader can see FY2027E 16,200kt is ~25% below the prior-year run-rate and that the cut tracks national quota discipline. (6) Minority bridge is under-deducted: Rp1,261.5bn of 30 June minority BOOK value is subtracted from a group DCF while 8.6% of group profit (Rp1,103.9bn in FY2026E) belongs to minorities - an implied 1.1x P/E on the minority stake; capitalising the minority claim at the group value would cut ~Rp280/share (6.3%). Offset by the conservative items below, so the target is still defensible, but fix it next run. (7) FY2026E delta-NWC of Rp7,170bn is mostly a re-basing from the pack historical NWC line (Rp4,210bn) to 10% of revenue (Rp11,379bn); the report stated FY2025 NWC of Rp8,458bn is not the model historical line - reconcile the basis (~Rp89/share, conservative). (8) The non-nickel block path escalates 2.0%/yr from FY2031 while the reporting-currency long-run inflation scalar is 2.5%, so the block slowly loses real ground against its own cost base; the basis says it escalates with reporting-currency inflation (~0.5pp/yr, conservative). (9) No peer-median cross-check is computed by the engine (lint: only 1 valuation method) while section 4 describes the two cross-checks as reported diagnostics - either restore them at 0% weight or state plainly they are not computed.
WATCH ITEMS: the ten-year ore life is the regulator NATIONAL saprolite statement (F42/S17) applied to the company, not a company reserve; it is disclosed, tested in the bull/bear and it cuts value, so it does not flatter the target. ANTM and NCKL are both BUY on the same reviewed nickel deck above spot - a shared house bet on Indonesian supply discipline, not a shared defect (ANTM is 100% DCF, NCKL is multiple-weighted).

bias.note: Base case reproduces the last actual: FY2026E EBITDA Rp17,406.5bn is 3.1% below the 9M2026 annualised Rp17,973bn (F14/S9); nickel and gold at the house decks, tax 19% and payout 70% at the LK rates, costs held in real terms, NWC at the FY2025 gross ratio. The one material departure from the last actual is the reserve-bounded volume (16,200kt FY2027E declining 8%/yr to zero after FY2036E), which is sourced to the regulator's sub-ten-year national saprolite life (F42/S17) and is the answer to the Q11 BLOCK, not a default haircut; the 16,200kt is 10% below the company's 18,000kt guidance (F30) and the report says so. Prudence sits in the 1.5pp state-control COE premium and the 13.5% unsourced royalty constant, both disclosed. Scenarios are mirrored on the same four drivers (nickel 0.8/1.25, volume 0.75/1.25, gold block 0.8/1.25, NWC 1.2/0.8) with base at 50%, and the bear at Rp3,355 is above the price, so the target is not a single bull assumption.

findings.finding: The report dismisses the pack's FY2025A EBITDA of Rp7,143.2bn on the ground that the year carries a D&A charge of Rp168.1bn that is roughly one-eleventh of the LK-implied annual charge (s1, s3, s4). D&A sits below EBITDA, so it cannot explain that line: the pack's FY2025A EBITDA is below the LK's 9M2025 EBITDA of Rp9,330bn (F43/S9), and the model's own FY2025A history is internally impossible - parent profit Rp7,208.8bn (confirmed by the Rp5,040bn 70% dividend, F18/S3) exceeds EBIT of Rp6,975.1bn at a 19% tax rate. The conclusion (do not anchor on the pack year) is right; the stated mechanism is not, and the trough-multiple argument rests on a number that is demonstrably wrong.

Section 2 says the house metals deck is above both spot prints and then quotes the deck's FY2025A marker of US$15,162/t, which is below both the US$15,400 (F38/S15) and US$16,375 (F37/S14) prints. The sentence contradicts its own numbers.
